## Background

<!-- CHANGE THIS -->

Hi! I’m currently a Master of City Planning student at the University of Pennsylvania, where I’m interested in the ways people and the environment interact. Before coming to Penn, I studied Environmental Science and Political Science at Villanova University, with a minor in Economics. My background has given me the opportunity to look at environmental and social issues from a few different perspectives, but GIS and spatial analysis have been what really helped bring those interests together.

Throughout my undergraduate research, I worked on projects involving wildfire vulnerability, climate change, coastal flooding, and environmental justice. I became interested in urban spatial analytics because I enjoy using data to understand why patterns occur in particular places and how those patterns affect different communities. 

As I continue my studies at Penn, I hope to build on these skills and learn how spatial analytics can be used to address real planning challenges. I’m particularly interested in climate resilience, land use, and environmental equity, and I hope to eventually use spatial analysis to help cities make more informed and equitable planning decisions.
